skill: Translate Newton's cooling statement into a differential equation for temperature approaching a fixed ambient temperature from above.
learner_operation: Identify the surrounding temperature as equilibrium, represent the temperature excess T-T_S, and choose a negative rate proportional to that excess with k>0; distinguish sign, equilibrium and spurious factors. Moderate cases also require ignoring the initial object temperature.
reasoning_steps: Read which temperature belongs to the environment
Match the resulting equation to a single radio choice
response_contract: One radio field with five math equations; no integration or numerical solution is asked. Canonical example has no captured bank.
difficulty: Easy cases provide only ambient temperature; moderate cases also give a hotter initial object temperature. Both stop at model selection.
invariants: Temperature decreases toward a fixed ambient value
No extra solving, integration, fitted k or new response type
permitted_variations: Ambient value and units within a plausible cooling scenario
Object/context and initial temperature above ambient where supplied
Derivative notation and correct option position
Algebraically equivalent representations of the same linear law can require reconsidering the sign and equilibrium; preserve method and workload
eligible_answer_assignments: Which numerical ambient value the model uses
Which option position contains the correct model
Which equivalent linear expression represents negative proportionality
essential_vs_incidental: Negative proportionality and the ambient role are essential. Specific ambient numbers, contexts, option positions and bank membership are incidental. The fact that canonical factored -k(T-a) is correct expresses the skill, not by itself an illicit shortcut. However a distinctive choice length, formatting or position may bypass it.
